title: Decision Making Warm Up - 4 Progressions
author: Kevin Galerno
description: Use the centre circle for four linked decision-making progressions. Start with low-pressure puck control, increase pressure, remove a puck so one player becomes the checker, then add outside passing options so players must scan, protect possession and make plays through pressure.
coaching_points: Eyes up and scan before pressure arrives.
Keep hands away from the body and move the puck outside the feet when protecting it.
Progress from recognizing the first layer of pressure to seeing the next layer and available passing lanes.

title: Awareness and Possession Progression
author: Kevin Galerno
description: F1 carries through the neutral zone while additional pressure is released in layers. Add an F4 support option to force both sides to scan away from the puck, communicate and make possession decisions as the pressure changes.
coaching_points: Exaggerate scanning so awareness becomes automatic.
Do not skate randomly - make decisions based on the next layer of pressure.
Use communication when the support player is added and continue until possession is lost.

title: NZ Loose Puck Retrieval Into OZ Entry
author: Kevin Galerno
description: F1 retrieves a loose puck near the far blue line under soft pressure and reads F2 as the entry option. F2 simultaneously reads F1 and the pressure from F4, then chooses the entry response. Progress by changing routes, puck locations and pressure layers.
coaching_points: Collect information before the retrieval or reception.
When turning from or into pressure, move the puck or the feet immediately.
Vary defender routes and pressure so the entry read stays game-like.

title: Long Rim Retrievals Into Quick Pass or Drive
author: Kevin Galerno
description: F1 enters under variable pressure, reads a long rim and locates F2 support. A second rim creates another retrieval under pressure, with F1 choosing a high or low escape before attacking a shooting lane. Add support or additional pressure as the read improves.
coaching_points: Use the puck's travel time on the rim to scan and collect information.
On rimmed pucks, keep the top hand up and the blade firm to prevent the puck from slipping underneath.
After the retrieval, move the puck or the feet immediately and communicate with support.
